subject: Biology
description: Photosynthesis: light, dark reactions, chlorophyll, products, key facts

questions.stem: PHOTOSYNTHESIS occurs primarily in which organelle of plant cell?
questions.explanation: CHLOROPLAST — green organelle in plant + algal cells. Contains: CHLOROPHYLL pigments (green; absorbs sunlight); STROMA (fluid; site of dark reactions / Calvin cycle); GRANA / THYLAKOIDS (membrane stacks; site of light reactions). Like mitochondria, chloroplasts have OWN DNA (cpDNA) — endosymbiotic origin (a primitive cyanobacterium engulfed by ancestral eukaryote ~1.5 BYA). NUMBER: typical leaf cell has 30-50 chloroplasts. INSIGHT — only PLANTS, ALGAE, CYANOBACTERIA photosynthesise. Animals don't (they consume plants/animals to get energy). Some special: corals + sea slugs host algae symbionts; sea slug Elysia chlorotica even retains chloroplasts from algae it ate ('solar-powered' slug).

questions.explanation: PHOTOSYNTHESIS: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + LIGHT → C₆H₁₂O₆ (glucose) + 6O₂. Inputs: CO₂ from air (via stomata), H₂O from soil (via roots), light energy from Sun. Outputs: GLUCOSE (energy storage, building block), O₂ (released into air). RESPIRATION = REVERSE — animals + plants both respire (use O₂ + glucose for energy). NET PLANTS → produce O₂; NET ANIMALS → consume O₂. WITHOUT photosynthesis, atmospheric O₂ would deplete in a few thousand years. INSIGHT — TWO STAGES: (1) LIGHT REACTIONS (in thylakoids; light splits H₂O → produces O₂, ATP, NADPH); (2) DARK REACTIONS / CALVIN CYCLE (in stroma; uses ATP+NADPH to fix CO₂ → glucose). Doesn't need darkness — runs in light too; just doesn't need light directly.

Emits green light from cells (option here)
Has green ions inside the cell (option here)

questions.explanation: CHLOROPHYLL — primarily absorbs RED + BLUE light, REFLECTS GREEN (which is why we see plants as green). The unabsorbed green wavelength bounces back to our eyes. INTERESTING evolutionary puzzle — why don't plants absorb the most abundant wavelength (green is mid-spectrum, sunlight peak there)? Hypothesis: chlorophyll evolved when atmosphere was different + early photosynthesisers used purple bacteriorhodopsin; chlorophyll filled niches AROUND. Also: green REFLECTANCE may protect against overheating. CHLOROPHYLL TYPES: Chl-a (universal), Chl-b (in green plants); both have a porphyrin ring with Mg²⁺ at centre (similar to haemoglobin's Fe). AUTUMN colours: chlorophyll breaks down → carotenoids (orange/yellow) + anthocyanins (red/purple) become visible.

questions.stem: STOMATA on plant leaves serve as:

options.option_text: Pores for gas exchange (CO₂ in, O₂ out)
Roots for water absorption from soil
Storage of starch in leaves (option here)

questions.explanation: STOMATA — small pores (mostly on UNDERSIDE of leaves; plural 'stomata', singular 'stoma'). Each surrounded by 2 GUARD CELLS that open/close. FUNCTION: gas exchange — CO₂ ENTERS (for photosynthesis); O₂ EXITS (by-product); water vapour exits (TRANSPIRATION). Open in DAY (need CO₂ for photosynthesis) + close at night (conserve water). DROUGHT response: stomata close to reduce water loss → also limits CO₂ uptake → photosynthesis slows. CAM PLANTS (cactus, agave, pineapple) — open stomata at NIGHT (cooler, less evaporation) + store CO₂ as malic acid; release for daylight photosynthesis — adaptation for dry climate. C4 plants (sugarcane, maize) also have specialised CO₂ concentration. Ordinary plants = C3.

questions.stem: OXYGEN released during photosynthesis comes from:
questions.explanation: Definitively from WATER. Proven by VAN NIEL (1930s, using sulfur bacteria — different photosynthetic process; analogous logic applied to plants) + ISOTOPIC tracing (HILL + RUBEN, 1941: ¹⁸O-labelled water → ¹⁸O₂ released; ¹⁸O-labelled CO₂ → no ¹⁸O₂; confirmed water source). PHOTOLYSIS / Hill reaction: 2H₂O + light + chlorophyll → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻. Splitting H₂O is the most energy-demanding part of photosynthesis. EARLY EARTH — no atmospheric O₂; photosynthesising cyanobacteria (~3 BYA onwards) gradually OXIDISED ocean iron (banded iron formations) → then atmosphere → 'GREAT OXIDATION EVENT' ~2.4 BYA. Made aerobic life possible. ALL atmospheric O₂ today (~21%) is biogenic.

questions.stem: MAJOR PIGMENT involved in photosynthesis is:
questions.explanation: CHLOROPHYLL-A — primary pigment; only one that DIRECTLY participates in light reactions (donates electrons to electron transport chain). Other pigments are 'ACCESSORY' / 'ANTENNA' pigments — absorb additional wavelengths + transfer energy to chlorophyll-a. ACCESSORY pigments: CHLOROPHYLL-B (broader absorption); CAROTENOIDS (β-carotene — orange, also vitamin A precursor; xanthophylls — yellow); PHYCOBILINS (in algae — red/blue). FUNCTION OF ACCESSORIES: (1) capture more wavelengths; (2) protect chlorophyll-a from photo-damage. REVEALED IN AUTUMN: chlorophyll-a degrades first → accessory pigments visible → leaves turn yellow/orange/red. APPLICATION — paper chromatography of leaf extract separates these pigments by colour bands (school experiment).

questions.stem: The CALVIN CYCLE (also called dark reaction or C3 cycle) takes place in:
questions.explanation: CALVIN CYCLE (Dark Reaction; named after MELVIN CALVIN, Nobel 1961) — happens in the STROMA (fluid matrix) of chloroplast. STAGES: (1) CARBON FIXATION — CO₂ + RuBP (5-C molecule) → 2 × 3-C molecules (3-PGA), catalysed by RuBisCO enzyme (most abundant protein on Earth!); (2) REDUCTION — using ATP + NADPH from light reactions, 3-PGA → G3P (glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate); (3) REGENERATION — most G3P regenerates RuBP; some G3P used to build glucose. Doesn't need light directly — uses ATP+NADPH. Whole cycle: 6 turns to produce 1 glucose. C4 + CAM plants have additional CO₂-concentrating mechanisms before Calvin cycle, more efficient in hot/dry conditions. RuBisCO is also the bottleneck of photosynthesis efficiency.
